identity.title: ALMA’s Polarized View of 10 Protostars in the Perseus Molecular Cloud

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present 870 $\mu$m ALMA dust polarization observations of 10 young Class 0/I protostars in the Perseus Molecular Cloud.

question.value: What is the origin of dust polarization (scattering, magnetically aligned grains, radiative alignment) on disk and envelope scales in Class 0/I protostars?

evidence.quote: Our principle survey goal was to examine the polarization structure of a set of young protostars to see whether we could explain it in the context of models that predict polarization due to different mechanisms
project code 2015.1.01503.S; P.I. Erin Cox
The data were taken using ALMA Band 7 on 2016, July 17 in configuration C40-4

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 continuum spectral windows centered on 337.5, 339.4, 347.5, 349.5 GHz; full polarization

evidence.quote: The 4 spectral windows were centered on 337.5, 339.4, 347.5, and 349.5 GHz.
in configuration C40-4
Baselines for the C40-4 configuration ranged from 15 to 704 meters
The typical resolution for our observations was 0.38$\ensuremath{''}$ by 0.31$\ensuremath{''}$.
corresponding to a maximum recoverable scale of $\sim 7.2 \ensuremath{''}$
The observations took a total of 2.6 hours, with $\sim$8 minutes spent per source.
The data were taken using ALMA Band 7 on 2016, July 17
project code 2015.1.01503.S; P.I. Erin Cox

provided.value: Sample selection and disk-candidate classification from 8 mm data

evidence.quote: Our target selection was constructed from our Very Large Array Nascent Disk and Multiplicity (VANDAM) survey
then chose the brightest 25 at 220 GHz from the Submillimeter Array (SMA) Mass Assembly of Stellar Systems and their Evolution (MASSES) survey
We also present the polarization properties and outflow angles (taken from (cite: st17), and references therein).

method.value: Form polarized intensity sqrt(Q^2+U^2), angle 0.5 arctan(U/Q), debias with mean Q/U noise, mask below 5 sigma, fraction = P/I

evidence.quote: The polarization intensity maps were debiased using the average noise value determined from the Q and U maps. Each map was masked below 5$\sigma$.
Each map was masked below 5$\sigma$.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure fluxes and mean polarization angle

method.value: Gaussian fits with imfit; polarized-intensity-weighted mean angle within 115 au (0.5 arcsec) radius of polarized peak

evidence.quote: The sum is taken within a circle of radius 115 au (= 0.5 arcsecond) centered at the peak of the polarized continuum.
Integrated and peak flux densities are estimated from elliptical Gaussian fits using the CASA task `imfit`.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare inner vs outer polarization fraction distributions

method.value: Kaplan-Meier estimator including upper limits, sampled at ~half-beam spacing; inner (~100-150 au) vs outer; log-rank test

evidence.quote: we sample the polarization fraction (or its upper limit) at spacings of $\sim 1/2$ beam-width (to ensure a degree of statistical independence).

validation.value: Checked detection threshold in outer regions; typical detection ~2x minimum threshold

evidence.quote: the typical detection is at a level $\sim$ 2 times the minimum detection threshold.

analysis_steps.goal: Test polarization offset from outflow axis

method.value: KS and AD tests against uniform distribution on 0-90 deg; disk-candidates vs non-disk-candidates

evidence.quote: We performed both the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) and Anderson-Darling (AD) tests to compare the distribution of $\Delta \theta$ to that of a uniform distribution.
using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package (cite: mc07), version 4.7.0
we used the `lifelines` Python package (cite: dp17)[^1] to compute the Kaplan-Meier product limit estimator
Matplotlib (http://dx.doi.org/10.1109/MCSE.2007.55)

results_numeric.quantity: Log-rank test p-value inner vs outer polarization fraction

evidence.quote: The p-value for the log-rank test between the two classes is $p \lesssim 10^{-4}$.

results_numeric.quantity: KS/AD p-value, disk-candidate offsets vs uniform

evidence.quote: We find suggestive evidence ($p \sim 0.02-0.06$) that the angular offset differs from a uniform random variable
We find no evidence ($p\gtrsim 0.3$) that the offset distribution for the non-disk-candidate sources is different from a random uniform distribution.

findings_qualitative.value: All sources polarized; 9/10 show extended polarized emission

evidence.quote: all of our sources show some degree of polarization, with most (9/10) showing significantly extended emission in the polarized continuum

claims.hypothesis: Inner (disk-scale) and envelope-scale polarization fractions are intrinsically different
claims.experiment: Kaplan-Meier CDFs with upper limits, log-rank test
claims.result: Outer regions more likely to show polarization above a few %; p≲1e-4
claims.finding: Different polarization mechanisms inner vs envelope

evidence.quote: the outer regions have a significantly higher chance of exhibiting a large value ($\gtrsim$ few %) as compared to the inner regions.

claims.hypothesis: Disk-candidate polarization is consistent with dust scattering
claims.experiment: Compare polarization angle to outflow axis/disk minor axis; KS and AD tests
claims.result: Disk-candidate vectors roughly along minor axis; offsets differ from uniform (p~0.02-0.06)
claims.finding: Consistent with self-scattering, though toroidal-field alignment is not excluded

evidence.quote: We find evidence that our disk-candidates show a polarization signature akin to either self-scattering in their inner region or grains aligned with a toroidal field in an inclined disk

why_this_data.value: Previous polarization surveys had poor resolution (>2.5 arcsec), causing disk/envelope confusion

evidence.quote: previous observations have not been able to disentangle them due to comparatively poor resolution

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot definitively state the cause of the polarization hole

evidence.quote: Though we cannot definitively state the cause of this hole, there are a few possibilities.

referee_caveats_inferred: Small sample (3 disk-candidates) limits the statistics
Disk-candidate classification relies on an unpublished thesis
Scattering vs toroidal-field alignment not distinguished
Single-band data cannot constrain grain sizes
